methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $70M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Neustark is a Series B climate and energy company founded by Valentin Gutknecht and Johannes Tiefenthaler that has raised $70M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set spanning 9 private companies and 1 public company (Linamar, ticker LNZA) operating in the Climate & Energy sector at Series B through Series C stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses the $70M raised as a proxy base value and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B advancement, implying a valuation of $133M. The peer-median approach examines three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: KoBold Metals ($3.0B, Series C), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B, Series C), and Amogy ($700M, Series C). The median of this set is $1.0B, with a range spanning $700M to $3.0B. These two methods—stage-progression and peer comparables—produce materially different signals, reflecting both early-stage uncertainty and wide dispersion in Climate & Energy valuations at this funding stage.

The triangulated analysis yields a range of $113M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $566M. Key uncertainties include the applicability of Series C peer valuations to a Series B stage company and the significant variance in public-market and private multiples within the Climate & Energy sector. Narrowing the range would require additional clarity on Neustark's unit economics, revenue trajectory, and technology differentiation relative to named comparables.
